t.6.71.1: While Lakṣmaṇa, devoted to his brother, was consoling Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa, having stationed the troops in their proper positions, came to that place.
t.6.71.2: He was surrounded by four heroic ministers bearing weapons of many kinds, like the leader of a herd encircled by elephants resembling heaps of dark collyrium.
t.6.71.3: Having approached the great-souled Rāghava, who was overwhelmed with grief, he saw the monkeys too, their eyes clouded with tears.
t.6.71.4: And he saw the great-souled Rāghava, the delight of the Ikṣvāku dynasty, fallen into a swoon and resting on the lap of Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.71.5: Seeing Rāma abashed and consumed by grief, Vibhīṣaṇa, his spirit downcast with inward sorrow, said, "What is this?"
t.6.71.6: Looking at the face of Vibhīṣaṇa, at Sugrīva, and at those vānaras, Lakṣmaṇa, his eyes flooded with tears, spoke these words.
t.6.71.7: O gentle one, as soon as Rāghava heard from Hanumān's words that Sītā had been slain here by Indrajit, he fell into a swoon.
t.6.71.8: But Vibhīṣaṇa, restraining Saumitri as he was speaking, addressed these words, rich in meaning, to Rāma, who had lost his senses.
t.6.71.10: But I know the intention of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa concerning Sītā, O mighty-armed one, and he will not bring about her killing.
t.6.71.9: O lord of men, what Hanumān told you in his distress, I consider as impossible as the drying up of the ocean.
t.6.71.11: Though he was entreated very many times by me, who wished to do him good, with the words "Let Vaidehī go," he did not act upon that advice.
t.6.71.12: Not by conciliation, not by sowing dissension, not by gifts, much less by battle, could she even be seen, nor indeed by any other means whatsoever.
t.6.71.13: Having bewildered the monkeys, that rākṣasa has gone back to the sanctuary called Nikumbhilā, where he will perform a fire-offering.
t.6.71.14: For once he has offered his oblations and come forth, this son of Rāvaṇa becomes unassailable in battle even by the gods together with Vāsava.
t.6.71.15: Surely, dear one, this illusion was employed by him to delude us, as he sought to obstruct the valor of the vānaras. Let us go there with our armies before it is completed.
t.6.71.17: Remain here, with your heart at ease and exalted in courage; send Lakṣmaṇa along with us, who will lead the army.
t.6.71.16: Tiger among men, cast off this grief that has come upon you without cause, for the whole army is losing heart at seeing you wasted by sorrow.
t.6.71.18: This tiger among men, with his sharpened arrows, will force that son of Rāvaṇa to abandon that rite, and then he will be slain.
t.6.71.19: These whetted, sharp arrows, fletched with the feathers of birds, fierce like birds of prey themselves, will drink his blood.
t.6.71.20: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, dispatch Lakṣmaṇa, who bears auspicious marks, for the destruction of the rākṣasa, just as the wielder of the thunderbolt sends forth his thunderbolt.
t.6.71.22: For once that lord of the rākṣasas has completed his rite, he becomes invisible in battle to gods and asuras alike; and when he who has completed his rite is eager to fight, even the gods would fall into grave peril.
t.6.71.21: O best of men, let there be no delay in the slaying of the enemy, which you are able to accomplish today. Release the word for the destruction of your foe, as great Indra did in crushing the cities of the Asuras.
